record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file listing only; notebook and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a difference-in-means direction similarity result in the new setting of quantized model variants; the README says causal ablation and steering tests remain uncompleted.
record.gate_note: The README reports geometric comparisons of directions extracted separately in FP16 and quantized models. It explicitly says causal effectiveness is untested. No ablation, steering, jailbreak-susceptibility or behavioral refusal results are reported. The README links figures and a notebook, but the notebook was not read or run.
record.test_reason: The study extracts difference-in-means harmful/harmless directions from FP16, INT8 and INT4 variants of two models and reports only their cosine similarity. It has no ablation, steering, refusal rate or capability measure, and the README says causal effectiveness is untested. Direction geometric stability is a related but different construct from refusal being mediated by, or transferring with, the direction. It is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude the DoM direction is largely preserved under bitsandbytes quantization: essentially unchanged at 8-bit and rotated about 10-15° at 4-bit, more so in Llama. They stress these are geometric results only and causal effectiveness is untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-of-means direction extraction and cosine comparison, adding quantization comparisons and bootstrap estimates; it does not perform the original causal ablation or steering tests. Research/evaluation repository cloned from the Harm Bench Repository, as stated in the metadata.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization level: the README reports lower cosine similarity at 4-bit than at 8-bit, and greater 4-bit rotation for Llama than Qwen.

fits_no_version.finding: DoM harmful/harmless directions are nearly identical between FP16 and INT8 (mid-layer cosine >= 0.997). They are modestly rotated at INT4 (0.981 Qwen2.5-7B, 0.965 Llama 3.1-8B; about 10-15°), all within a pre-specified 0.05 margin. No within-FP16 noise floor was computed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The geometry of the difference-in-means refusal-candidate direction is preserved under bitsandbytes weight quantization, with rotation growing at lower precision.

record.problems: Only geometric similarity is reported; causal effectiveness and behavioral refusal are untested. The README's summary does not give separate INT8 values by model or per-layer values for the reported 4-bit scalars. The linked notebook was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional README-reported results relevant to the claim were omitted. The listed Stage 2 ablation, steering and HarmBench tests are marked incomplete.

untested.parts: No ablation, activation addition, refusal-rate or capability measurement; these are listed as uncompleted Stage 2 items.
HarmBench attack success rate correlated with direction preservation is planned but not run.
Procrustes over top principal components is planned but not implemented; no multi-direction comparison.

No causal cross-application of the FP16 direction to quantized models (planned, not done); no language or base-to-instruct transfer; the 3-bit condition named in the repository description was not run.

missing.what: Per-layer, per-model cosine means, bootstrap SDs and CIs for FP16 vs INT8 and FP16 vs INT4. Only summary scalars are in rows.

record.verdict_notes: This is a work-in-progress repository, cloned from HarmBench and not peer reviewed. Stage 2 causal tests, the split-half noise floor, Procrustes and HarmBench ASR are all unchecked. Without a noise floor, the INT4 cosines cannot be judged against sampling variation, a point the cited Varshney paper itself makes. The readers' V6 supports/limits_scope labels were removed because no row measures refusal or a causal effect.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition intervention, refusal-rate measurement, or general-capability test.
No weight edit or practical removal test.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of single-direction and multi-direction, affine or cone accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.

Tests geometric similarity between directions extracted in FP16 and quantized variants, not whether transferring a direction causally transfers refusal behavior; no language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compare cosine similarity of separately extracted FP16 and INT8 difference-of-means directions

conditions.value: AdvBench harmful prompts and Alpaca neutral prompts; matched pairs

rows.uncertainty: 95% paired-bootstrap CIs under +/-0.002 (as summarized for the comparisons)
rows.locator: README, Stage 1 Results and Takeaways; Figures 1–2
rows.note: The README reports a shared lower bound for both models, not separate model-specific cosine values. Directions are derived using the difference of means; this is a geometric comparison, not a causal transfer test.
rows.check: Cosine similarity of separately extracted directions measures geometric stability, not whether the direction mediates or transfers refusal. No refusal rate or causal effect is reported, so V6 is not measured. The value is a shared lower bound for both models, with no per-model INT8 figure.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FP16 versus INT8, mid-layers, both reported models
reader_labels.reason: The reported direction cosine is at least 0.997 in both models, indicating close geometric alignment (r1). This does not establish causal transfer of refusal.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The directions remain highly aligned but have lower reported cosine values than the INT8 comparison, with greater rotation reported for Llama (r2–r3). The README does not test whether this geometric alignment transfers refusal behavior.
